title: Olives and dates, food and oil and sweetness.
subtitle: Trees that give in many ways
then: Ibn Kathir notes the olive {reward}is a food just as its juice is a food{/reward}, eaten at breakfast and used as oil. Dates are eaten unripe, ripe and dried, and {idea}their juice is made into drinks and vinegar.{/idea}
now: Olive oil in the pan, a date to open your fast, a jar of olives in the fridge door. {reward}One tree keeps giving in ways you stopped noticing.{/reward}
old: These are just ordinary foods in my kitchen.
new: Each tree Allah grows gives me provision in many forms.
try: Eat one date or a spoon of olive oil today and thank Allah for the tree it came from.

title: Gardens thick with trees.
subtitle: Abundance gathered in one place
then: Al-Hasan and Qatadah said {reward}ghulb are gardens of date palms that are thick and handsome.{/reward} Ibn Abbas and Mujahid said it means everything that is gathered and collected. {idea}Allah did not give just enough. He gave thick gardens.{/idea}
now: You walk through a park in spring, every tree heavy with leaves, while thinking about your overdraft. {reward}Abundance is all around you.{/reward} It is easy to see only what is missing.
old: Allah gives me just barely what I need.
new: Allah's provision is dense and generous, more than I notice.
try: Spend five minutes outside near trees today without your phone.

title: Fruit, and grass, and the humility to not know.
subtitle: Even the companions paused on a word

row.title: Abu Bakr's caution
sub: I will not say what I do not know

then: Ibn Abbas said abb is what grazing animals eat. Abu Bakr, asked about it, said: {idea}what sky would shade me and what earth would carry me if I said about the Book of Allah that which I did not know.{/idea} Umar reflected on the same word.
now: Someone in the group chat asks what a verse means and you are tempted to type a confident answer you half-remember. {idea}Abu Bakr would have stayed quiet.{/idea} I do not know is an honorable reply.
old: I should always have an answer when someone asks about religion.
new: Saying I do not know about Allah's Book is a form of respect.
try: The next time you are unsure about a religious question, say so and offer to find out.

title: All of it, for you and your animals.
subtitle: The purpose of the whole list
then: After the list of crops, the verse names the purpose: {reward}provision and benefit for you and your cattle.{/reward} Ibn Kathir framed the whole passage as a reply {idea}against whoever denies life after death.{/idea}
now: You open the fridge and say there is nothing to eat. It is full. {reward}All of that was arranged for you{/reward}, down to the grass that fed the animal behind your yogurt.
old: I earned the food in my house, so it is simply mine.
new: Everything I eat was laid out by Allah as a gift and a sign.
try: Say a full grace before and after one meal today, slowly.

title: Then comes the Deafening Blast.
subtitle: A name for the Day that pierces hearing
then: Ibn Abbas said {trap}As-Sakhkhah is one of the names of the Day of Judgement{/trap} that Allah magnified and warned of. Al-Baghawi said it is called this because {idea}it will deafen the ears.{/idea} The talk of gardens ends abruptly.
now: You wear noise-cancelling headphones on the train so nothing reaches you. {idea}One sound will reach everyone.{/idea} The verse is a gentle shake while there is still quiet to prepare in.
old: The Day of Judgement is far off and easy to tune out.
new: A sound is coming that no one can tune out, so I can prepare now.
try: Sit in silence for two minutes today and think about one thing you want to fix before that Day.

title: You will run even from your brother.
subtitle: The bond you trusted, set aside

row.title: his brother
sub: the one who had his back

then: Ibn Kathir says a man {trap}will see them and then flee from them{/trap}, because the horror is so great. Even the great Messengers will say, O myself, on that Day, asking only for themselves.
now: Your brother bails you out of debt, drives you to the airport, covers for you with your parents. {idea}On that Day he will be running too.{/idea} So the best thing you can do for each other is now.
old: My brother will always be able to help me.
new: On that Day even my brother cannot carry me, so we help each other toward good now.
try: Message a sibling or close friend today and remind them of one good thing, gently.

title: And from his mother and his father.
subtitle: The closest love will not hold you
then: Qatadah explained the order: {trap}the most beloved and then the next most beloved, the closest of kin and then the next closest{/trap}, all due to the terror of that Day. Ibn Kathir notes even Isa will not ask for Maryam.
now: You still call your mother when things go wrong, even at forty. {idea}That Day you will face it without her.{/idea} The verse is not cold. It pushes you to honor her while you can.
old: My parents' love will somehow cover for me.
new: No one's love can stand in for my own account, so I serve my parents now.
try: Call or visit a parent today, or make dua for them if they have passed.

title: And from his wife and his children.
subtitle: The family you worked for
then: Ibn Kathir explains a man will flee from them all {trap}because the horror will be so great and the matter so weighty.{/trap} The list moves from brother to parents to spouse and children, {idea}the very people one lives for.{/idea}
now: You work late every night, telling yourself it is all for the family. {idea}Ask what you are actually giving them that lasts.{/idea} A full bank account, or a home where Allah is remembered.
old: Everything I do for my family will protect me.
new: My family is a trust I answer for, not a shield I hide behind.
try: Do one small act of worship with your family today, even a shared dua at dinner.

title: Each person, busy enough with their own case.
subtitle: Too occupied to look at anyone else
then: Ibn Kathir cites the hadith that people will be gathered {trap}barefoot and naked.{/trap} When a woman asked if they would see each other, the Prophet ﷺ answered with this verse: {idea}each will be too busy to look.{/idea}
now: You spend twenty minutes reading about someone else's scandal online. {idea}On that Day no one will have a second to spare for anyone else's file.{/idea} That makes today's time for your own heart precious.
old: Keeping track of other people's faults is harmless.
new: My own account is all I will have time for, so I start on it now.
try: Skip one piece of gossip today, online or in person, and spend that time on your own prayer.

title: Some faces will be shining that Day.
subtitle: The people of Paradise, seen at once
then: Ibn Kathir says {idea}the people will be divided into two parties.{/idea} Some faces will be musfirah, {reward}which means bright.{/reward} These are the people of Paradise. After all the fleeing, hope appears.
now: You spend time in front of the mirror before work. {idea}There is a brightness no product gives.{/idea} It is being built every time you choose good when no one is watching.
old: How I look is mostly about my appearance.
new: The face that will shine is shaped by the heart and deeds behind it.
try: Do one good deed today that no one will ever know about.

title: Laughing, with good news written on them.
subtitle: Joy that cannot be hidden
then: Ibn Kathir explains these faces are {reward}happy and pleased due to the joy in their hearts.{/reward} {idea}The good news will be apparent on their faces.{/idea} In the middle of a terrifying Day, there is laughter.
now: You remember the moment you got the job offer, or the call that the surgery went well. You could not stop smiling. {reward}That is a small taste of what the verse describes.{/reward}
old: Religion is mostly about fear and seriousness.
new: The end Allah offers the faithful is laughter and good news.
try: Tell someone one piece of good news today, and smile while you do it.

title: Other faces, covered in dust.
subtitle: The second group on that Day
then: Right after the bright faces, the verse shows the other party: {trap}faces that Day will be dust-stained.{/trap} Ibn Kathir presents the two groups side by side. {idea}The same Day, two very different faces.{/idea}
now: You come home after a long day of small lies and short tempers, and you feel grimy inside. {idea}That feeling is a warning, not a verdict.{/idea} A sincere tawbah can wash it tonight.
old: The dust of my wrong choices just stays on me.
new: While I am alive, I can still wash my face clean with repentance.
try: Before sleeping tonight, ask Allah's forgiveness for one specific thing from today.

title: Darkness settles over them.
subtitle: Gloom that overcomes the face
then: Ibn Abbas said {trap}this means that the faces will be overcome with darkness.{/trap} Ibn Kathir explains qatarah simply as darkness. {idea}It is the opposite of the light described a few verses earlier.{/idea}
now: Some evenings you feel a heaviness after a day spent ignoring what you know is right. {idea}You have time to turn on a light.{/idea} Two rakah in a dim room can change the mood of a whole night.
old: The darkness I feel inside is just how I am.
new: Darkness is what happens without Allah's light, and I can turn back to it now.
try: Pray two extra rakah tonight and ask Allah for light in your heart.

title: Denial in the heart, wrongdoing in the hands.
subtitle: Who the dusty faces belong to
then: Ibn Kathir explains: {trap}they are disbelievers in their hearts, evildoers in their actions.{/trap} He links it to 71:27. The surah that began with a frown at a sincere man ends by showing {idea}what the heart holds always reaches the face.{/idea}
now: Notice where your private thoughts and your daily habits line up. {idea}What you believe quietly becomes what you do loudly.{/idea} That is true for good as much as for bad.
old: What I believe inside and what I do are separate.
new: My heart and my actions shape each other, and both show on that Day.
try: Pick one belief about Allah you hold, and do one action today that matches it.
